files.about: Requirements R1-R27 (0.2: event shards, replay, experiments, surveys; 0.3: actions, cohorts, heatmaps, SQL, local evaluation, continuity, survey targeting, replay settings, no row limits; 0.4: optional Basin / Iceberg cold tier queried from SQL) with acceptance checks, scope and definition of done.

The normative SDK wire format: capture routes, body decoding, tokens, timestamps, v1 capture, persons and merges, feature flags, remote config, replay snapshots and settings, surveys and targeting, exposure, heatmaps, local evaluation, experience continuity, error codes.
Worked examples for decoding, tokens, timestamps, distinct ids, flag hashing and matching, capture responses and person scenarios.

Stack, storage and event-shard decisions, Cloudflare config, deploy and upgrade, data model, ingestion, query semantics, actions, cohorts, SQL, heatmaps, streaming funnels, replay, experiment statistics, surveys, owner API, screens, tests, limits and the Basin cold tier (stream, Iceberg sink, Basin SQL compiler, retention).
Build order, each step with a check.
How the protocol was established with REA (0.1-0.3 captures, 0.4 Basin findings, and conformance runs), evidence and obligation ledgers, unknowns, licensing and choices.

changelog.note: A Worker can serve extra hostnames, such as a first-party ingest subdomain on the measured site: SDK endpoints, /static and /_health answer on every host, while dashboard pages redirect to SITE_URL and other owner API writes there get 421, so sign-in and cookies stay on one origin. No config change.

Optional cold tier on Cloudflare Basin: every ingested event is also streamed through a Basin Pipelines Worker binding into an Apache Iceberg table in R2 (Basin Catalog), and the SQL editor gains a Cold source that compiles the same query language to Basin SQL with the project and retention filters always applied. Off unless the COLD_STREAM binding, BASIN_* vars and BASIN_TOKEN secret are set; upgrades a 0.3 instance in place (no D1 migration).

Actions (CSS selector, text, href, URL matchers), static and dynamic cohorts usable as filters in insights, flags, surveys and experiments, click/rage/dead-click/mouse-move heatmaps and scroll depth over the live page or a recording, a read-only SQL editor across shards, posthog-node local evaluation, experience continuity, survey targeting/iterations/partial responses, replay sampling/triggers/network/console/canvas settings with paged playback, and streaming funnels and surveys without row limits. Upgrades a 0.2 instance in place (D1 0003, hourly cron).

Session replay (posthog-js recorder, R2 chunks, rrweb-player), experiments (multivariate flags, Bayesian results), surveys (posthog-js /api/surveys, results) and time-sharded event storage past 10 GB per project with exact counts. Upgrades a 0.1 instance in place.
posthog-js is credited with its actual licence (Apache-2.0 and MIT). The e2e flag check waits for the flags reload after identify, so it also passes against a deployed instance over the network.
